newsitem.title: INDIA: India tea auction prices dipping - Tata Tea.
newsitem.headline: India tea auction prices dipping - Tata Tea.

text.p: India's leading tea firm Tata Tea Ltd said on Thursday it expected the current downtrend in Indian tea auction prices to continue for the next few months.

"Unlike last year, tea prices in the auctions have shown a declining trend from September 1996 as a consequence of export demand compression," chairman Ratan Tata said in a statement issued after a board meeting to finalise accounts.

"This trend is likely to continue for the next few months as a result of which profit margings on the plantation operations, particularly in the south, during the second half of the current year are likely to be lower, compared to the corresponding period of last year," it said.
Tata Tea said its overall turnover rose by 40 percent for the first six months of 1996/97 (April-March). The turnover on core operations rose by 21 percent over the previous year.

Tata Tea achieved a record export turnover of 1.05 billion rupees. Core export operations jumped 70 percent. Exports of traded coffee, on which the profit margins are lower, also rose substantially, it said.
The company, part of the house of Tatas, India's largest business house, announced a net profit of 353 million rupees for the first half of 1996/97, up from 283.1 million in the year ago period.
